html:
The Battles of Khalkhin Gol were fought from May to September 1939 on Mongolia's eastern border with Japanese-run Manchukuo, between Soviet and Mongolian forces and the Japanese army.

A dispute over the border along the Khalkhin river grew into a real war. In August the Soviet commander Georgy Zhukov used tanks, aircraft and infantry together to surround and destroy the Japanese force. A ceasefire was agreed in September, just after the Second World War began in Europe.

The defeat persuaded Japan's leaders not to attack the Soviet Union again. They turned south, toward the oil of the Dutch East Indies, which led to Pearl Harbor. Stalin could later move troops from the east to defend Moscow. For Mongolia it secured the eastern border.
sum: The Battles of Khalkhin Gol were fought from May to September 1939 on Mongolia's eastern border with Japanese-run Manchukuo, between Soviet and Mongolian forces and the Japanese army.
